customize.text: Avrelian
Sacred Heir

More than six thousand years ago, in the golden kingdom of Hyperborea, people launched the "Elysium Project." They hoped to transform the world into an Elysium for humankind alone. After relentless experimentation, they mastered the power of tailoring and refining the Seeds of Life. The new humans born after such "adjustments" were supposed to wield elemental forces at will. They hoped that their descendants would produce enough food to free all life from hunger, unlock primordial secrets, and freely transform matter into energy and vice versa. When the golden kingdom was destroyed, the survivors traveled south, where they settled on Hiisi Island and became the Frostmoon Scions. The Hyperboreans left behind a supremely advanced device: the Subatomic Assembling Mass-Energy Patterning Orb, later known as the Sampo Mill. It was designed to reconstruct matter at the subatomic scale, that is, or to transmute matter directly into stable energy. Although its structure remained largely intact, the device was unusable because the collaborative control module connected to the device was lost during the fall of Hyperborea and couldn't be replicated with existing technologies. After the discussion, it was decided to seal the device indefinitely without re-evaluating its feasibility. The SAMPO gradually transformed from a device into a religious symbol. They believed that only the heir foretold in the prophecy, who wielded the elements, could awaken the Mill and create an Elysium of eternal abundance for them. To create the ideal heir, the Frostmoon Scions continued the
of the Hyperborean era. Since the core processes, including the process of creating Fae and editing the Seeds of Life, were lost during the fall of Hyperborea, it was decided to purify the blood of the Frostmoon Scions through controlled selection. It was assumed that this would result in the birth of the prophesied Sacred Heir, who would freely command the pure, unaltered elemental forces at will, without resorting to ritual implements or sacrificing their soul, thereby achieving fusion with the world.

Several millennia later, a blessed maiden was born who, according to the prophecy, was destined to bear the sacred heir. But when the girl met a young man from the northern kingdom, she felt a love she had never felt before and abandoned her mission for the sake of the young officer. For this new feeling, this foolishness called love, she cut off her antlered crown and threw it onto the snowy ground. She wanted her unborn son, Avrelian, to live in peace and joy, never to set foot on the lands of Nod-Krai or believe in dreams of "Elysium." Though she had long since left her homeland, the new life growing within her awakened long-dormant visions of the fall of civilizations and the future of her homeland. She saw how humans first enjoyed wisdom and prosperity, followed by greed and selfish desires, each masked by noble names. From them followed hatred, curses, betrayal, strife, plunder, slaughter, and kin turning against kin. Cities were scattered across the land, some following the path of good, others the path of evil, and the divine envoys remained silent and did not interfere. But when the kings of men dared to test the
the great towers fell in flames. Like all tragic illusions, this boundless Elysium would crumble. The dying world drew near its end, and only the shadows of the past remained in its halls. But Avrelian's voice, which she had never heard before, full of compassion as soft as light, always whispered to her from the dead end of darkness and pain: <color=#ffffffd9>"I shall bring an end to the warriors of this land and raise a boundless Elysium in their place. I do this not to be king, but so that no other can ever claim that role."</color>

When spies were sent to retrieve the blessed maiden and return her to the homeland she was meant to love, the girl saw her lover's blood spilling beneath her feet and slit her throat. The Frostmoon Scions did not know that she had given birth to a son, Avrelian, and after his parents' deaths, he was adopted by a private officer named Mikhnenko, which allowed the boy to enroll in the Snezhnayan Royal Military Academy. But shortly after Avrelian was promoted to officer, he was marked as "died in the line of duty," as part of a plot hatched by Professor Rotwang of the Belyi Tsar's court and Alvis, Grand Duke of Kitezhgrad. Avrelian later returned to Nod-Krai and became the great thief Reed Miller. The professor once saw a pitch-black Elysium beyond the heavens and resolved to do everything in his power to reach it. When the Belyi Tsar sent him to Nod-Krai on a secret mission to retrieve a treasure hidden there that could upend the world, Rotwang chose to seize it not to save the world, but to use it as a means to his own ends. He believed that only those like him and Avrelian, chosen by a higher grace, were worthy of living on. It was better to find liberation by sacrificing oneself for a greater purpose than to remain lost in endless cycles of reincarnation.

<color=#ffffffd9>"Reed Miller, cast your meaningless melancholy aside, for you and I have been chosen by fate."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Come, follow me. Though the world is destined for destruction, we shall emerge from the celestial shell!"</color>

And although the professor promised Avrelian an Elysium, that world was never Avrelian’s dream. From the very beginning, Rotwang used the sacred heir only to obtain the Sampo Mill for himself. And the Elysium he spoke of was intended for him alone.

customize.text: Reed Miller

Since childhood, Avrelian had been friends with Solovei, a member of the noble Snezhnaya family whose emblem was the nightingale. Avrelian once carved the first raven emblem, imitating the nightingale, which later became the symbol of the Treasure Hoarders. As a child, Avrelian often spoke of his dream of creating an "Elysium" on earth and railed against the gods and the rich. One day, Avrelian and Solovei persuaded Governor Prokhor Trubetskoy's five-year-old adopted son, Brahe, to reveal the location of his father's treasure. They played good cop and bad cop, using both the carrot and the stick to get him to talk, and Avrelian distributed the stolen wealth to the children of Nod-Krai. But they never learned that Trubetskoy had managed to recoup three times the amount in less than three days.

<color=#ffffffd9>"It's a place my brothers and sisters remain — where they continue to endure hardships they should never have to bear. Tell me, those innocent souls — were they born to suffer like this?</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>If it's the law that is causing their suffering, then I shall rewrite the law. And if it's the corrupt nobles, then I shall purge them from their ranks!</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>One day, I'll raise an Elysium that belongs to us on this land — a land that has always belonged to us!"</color>

When Avrelian took the name Reed Miller and returned to Nod-Krai, he decided to create an "Elysium" for everyone. He gathered the outcasts and the wretched under the wings of a black raven, and thus the first Treasure Hoarders were born. At the time, they called him their leader, believing that this young man of unknown origin could break the shackles and build an equal Elysium for all who suffered. Reed Miller forged the first iron coin engraved with the raven symbol, which became the first true "Iron Coin." Later, raven seals were used to identify Treasure Hoarders and determine their status. In a world without borders, in a paradise where no one suffers from hunger or cold, the gold bestowed and governed by the Deus Auri was never meant to serve as the foundation of human cooperation. Humans should be masters of money, not its servants. Even if no one can claim the heart of gold for themselves, everyone should be able to wield the wealth that inherently belongs to everyone. Rumor had it that Reed Miller created a set of tools, dubbed the "Seven Tools of the Great Thief," to destroy artificial boundaries, be they chains or state borders. The great thief was caught numerous times, but each time he escaped punishment.

<color=#ffffffd9>"To the poor, to the hungry, to the cold, to the oppressed, and the abused. To my brothers and sisters, all of you who have found your way here..."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"If you have ever suffered injustice at the hands of fate, or if you have ever wept through the night for your neighbor's pain and suffering..."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"If you, too, long for a refuge without fear, and if you, too, dream of a world where no tears are shed,"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Then you, too, must break free of your chains and join us, your brothers and sisters."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Let the dead bury the dead, and rise to build an Elysium for the hungry and the poor on the wealth of the high and haughty."</color>

When Reed Miller infiltrated the Frostmoon Scions to obtain the Sampo Mill, he met twin sisters, Aila and Alia, who were destined to give birth to the perfect heir. Alia, unwilling to accept such a fate, fled with Avrelian, joining the Treasure Hoarders. He swore to her never to put himself in danger or break that oath. When his friend, Solovei, convinced Avrelian to leave the Treasure Hoarders and go to Snezhnograd to explain himself to the Belyi Tsar, Avrelian begged Alia not to fear for him and not to shed tears for the future, for it has not yet arrived. <color=#ffffffd9>"I know you have your doubts about my friend, but please trust my plan for now. Do not worry about me, Alia. If I am indeed the prophesied Ruler of Elysium, then no fate in this world can tear me from the brethren I hold dear."</color> These were the great thief's last words to the world. In Snezhnograd, he wasn't even allowed to see the Tsar and was sent straight to the scaffold. And although Avrelian's life was over, Reed Miller's name lived on.

customize.text: Alia

When Alia fled the Frostmoon Scions with Reed Miller, they regarded her as a traitor, and her name was forgotten. After Avrelian's death, Alia donned a silver mask and claimed to be the "master thief Reed Miller who had escaped the gallows." Over the centuries, many theories have accumulated about why the great thief hid his face. Some say he did what he did to keep himself safe from the relentless searches happening in Snezhnaya, while others say that he wore a mask to hide certain marks that had been left on him by the executioner. Some tales claim the master thief put on the mask after growing weary of the love or hate of the madding crowd, and that his close shave with death had left him a changed man — taciturn and sparing with his words. Some believed the mask concealed a face as beautiful as the court Fae. No matter the truth, the master thief's silver mask has become a symbol of the great thief. Alia molded the Treasure Hoarders into a highly disciplined, quasi-military force that almost resembled a religious order. Her mantra was that no one should place their faith in gods or deities, for it was humanity alone that held the power to save its own. The Treasure Hoarders of that era could be described as "an irreligious religious order." Under the name "Reed Miller," she gathered a large group of bandits, and together, they picked the governor's palace in Nod-Krai clean in a single night. All the countless curios, antiques, Mora, and jewels that they made off with were given by Alia to the poor of Nasha Town. Although the Treasure Hoarders had distanced themselves from Avrelian's dream of Elysium, and for the people, those ideals and Elysium were as distant as the moon in the sky, the great thief Reed Miller began to be revered in Nod-Krai. Perhaps they dreamed of someone like Alia, who could scatter riches directly into their hands, without any effort on their part.

<color=#ffffffd9>"Laugh at their fearful lies, brethren. For they cannot kill Reed Miller, the master thief."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"They have but murdered a single crow, but with tomorrow's light, a murder of crows shall rise to be at my back."</color>

After Avrelian's death, when Alia became the new Reed Miller, Solovei arrived in Nod-Krai and began to interfere with Professor Rotwang's plans. Although Alia distrusted Solovei, she knew that using the Sampo Mill would pose great danger, so she pretended to be his close friend to gain his trust and set off with him. When Professor Rotwang built a heaven-reaching tower in Nod-Krai, named the Pillar of Embla, he intended to use the Sampo Mill to siphon the land's power and, through that tower, ascend to the "Elysium" he believed lay beyond the sky. Had his scheme succeeded, all of Nod-Krai — its soil and every living being upon it — would have become fuel for his ascent. Alia and Solovei did everything they could to stop him, but at the time, they were too weak. When they reached the Pillar of Embla, Rotwang was one step away from his goal. Realizing there was no other choice, Alia cast herself into the Sampo Mill and, with her own body, ignited it with the purified blood of the Frostmoon Scions. Alia's sacrifice thwarted the Professor's plans and destroyed him for the first time.

customize.text: Brahe

Brahe was the adopted son of the Fae Lord Prokhor Trubetskoy, ruler of all of Nod-Krai. Some claimed he was actually the governor's illegitimate son, and because he had Fae blood in his veins, he was more handsome than most humans. Like Avrelian, he attended the Military Academy, though he enrolled long after Avrelian had graduated. After graduating, Brahe returned to Nod-Krai, where, like all the other nobles of Snezhnaya at the time, he indulged in a life of excess and pleasure. This continued until one night, when he saw Alia robbing the governor's palace and fell in love with her at first sight. He was so captivated by her that he even abandoned his noble life to join the Treasure Hoarders. Brahe inherited the Grand Duke title from his adoptive father, but when Solovei the Torchforger asked the Tsaritsa to grant the borderlands autonomy, Grand Duke Brahe also appeared before the throne. There, he willingly gave up any claim to the land and all it held. He then entrusted the governor's palace to the Lightkeepers, who turned it into a military fortress. After the death of his beloved, Brahe adopted the name Reed Miller and continued robbing the rich to help the poor and the people of Nod-Krai. Brahe believed that it was impossible to force a person who had never known kindness, who had suffered humiliation all his life, to believe that he should love his neighbor and his enemy. What he saw robbed him of his idealistic faith in human nature and the dream of an Elysium for all.

After Professor Rotwang's death, he was left with followers who faithfully continued to serve the professor. One of these followers was Inspector R. M. Morozov, who built a bunker to protect against the apocalypse on Wavechaser Plain. Although Morozov claimed the bunker served as protection from the forces of the Abyss, he was actually awaiting Rotwang's return and conducting experiments specifically for this purpose. Families with children gathered in the shelter, all believing the world outside had been destroyed by the apocalypse, preventing them from leaving. Under Morozov's orders, Senior Researcher Grazyna Myklukho conducted experiments with kuuvahki, as some studies indicated that prior to the apocalypse, kuuvahki exerted a catalytic effect on the growth of certain plants, inducing developmental mutations that result in phenotypes more attuned to kuuvahki. By artificial regulation of the mutation process, Grazyna was able to develop special plants, which Brahe, who had infiltrated the bunker, later named Mandragora. Grazyna submitted a request to upgrade the existing ventilation system by installing a pipeline to carry kuuvahki, circulated by the plants, and Morozov agreed. Grazyna didn't suspect that this system could be used not only for kuuvahki but also to amplify Abyssal pollution, creating the illusion of a destroyed world. The researcher hoped that one day, people would emerge to the surface and find a new world, and that her plants would help them rid themselves of the black filth. Gradually, due to the Abyssal leak and the escaped Abyssal monsters, people began to die. Grazyna asked Morozov to immediately cease all further testing of the purification system and destroy all living specimens from the Abyss, but he refused. Senior Mechanic Kotelnikov discovered Morozov's true motives and passed the information on to Grazyna so she could save the children. Furthermore, Brahe left her a message that if she wished to leave the bunker, she was to hand over an item to any of the Treasure Hoarders, and they would lead her to the great thief Reed Miller. When the researcher learned of what was happening, she asked Brahe to secretly remove the children from the facility. He said he knew an eccentric old hunter, probably Sukhotin, who was an old acquaintance of the Frostmoon Scions' Moonchanter. Together with Brahe, Grazyna managed to destroy Morozov and seal the bunker, but Brahe warned her that the Abyssal contamination in these parts could not be eradicated overnight, and that Morozov would one day rise as a mad monster, only to be destroyed by the hero of the prophecy of the Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions. Until then, he would forever wander these Abyss-corroded ruins, devouring the flesh and blood of those who stray in here. As Brahe had predicted, Morozov returned as the Ultimate Calamity, believing the world to be destroyed, having broken free of the heavenly shell and no longer bound by gravity or the laws of fate. The Ultimate Calamity was destroyed by the Traveler and Paimon, who had entered the bunker.

Ten years after Alia's sacrifice, the Treasure Hoarders had scattered across the globe, justifying their atrocities against the innocent with the words of Reed Miller. Whether it's wandering merchants barely scraping by, or overworked laborers starving for their next meal, anyone could be branded a "lackey of princes" or a "traitor who betrays his brothers and neighbors," and therefore "ripe for their noble robbery." Those who came before overcame evil with noble ideals, but now, the bandits waved the same banner, declaring that anyone who opposes them is an enemy of those noble ideals, thus embodying the very evil that was once defeated. And though Brahe fought the bandits who committed evil in Reed Miller's name, oppressing the laboring poor by sending them to the Eye of Kratti to sleep with fishes for good, he feared what would become of the Treasure Hoarders after his death. No one could guarantee that their once-noble ideals wouldn't be distorted beyond recognition, that crimes he couldn't even imagine wouldn't be committed under their guise. Brahe couldn't place all his hopes on human nature, for humans breed evil as naturally as bees produce honey. He didn't want Reed Miller's name to fade into the stream of history and be forgotten, or for that name and the ideals it once represented to be distorted by villains in future generations and cursed by humanity. So he decided to bury so-called ideals in history, smothering them with countless contradictory, absurd, laughable yet irresistible stories, until every trace of meaning is worn away and only a sweeping legend remains. This way, anyone who commits evil in our name will never be mistaken for a serious idealist, but rather a childish dreamer lost in their romantic tales. And as long as the legends of the Great Treasure live, gamblers dreaming of making a fortune overnight will repeat the name of the "Master Thief Reed Miller" again and again. If the rebels of the future truly need a new banner, they would find their hero, and his name may be anything but "Master Thief Reed Miller. After Brahe, many tried to call themselves Reed Miller, but no one else's name has survived into history.
